display.title: Asarah B'Teves: A Time to Remember the Siege of Yerushalayim
display.summary_short: Why we remember the tenth of Teves: the siege of Yerushalayim that led to the Churban, and how Torah and mitzvos keep us safe under Hashem's protection.
display.summary_long: A calendar talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Teves is the fourth month of the Jewish year and that something sad happened in it. Quoting Shlomo HaMelech, 'there is a time for everything', he teaches that although we serve Hashem with joy, there is also a time to be sad, not to stay sad but to learn from the past and improve ourselves. On the tenth of Teves the armies of Nevuchadnetzar, king of Bavel, surrounded Yerushalayim and sealed its gates; the trapped people grew weak from hunger. After two and a half years the walls were breached on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and three weeks later, on Tisha B'Av, the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed. We ask what caused this and how to prevent it: as long as we learn Torah and keep its mitzvos, no power can harm us, for, as Dovid HaMelech wrote, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
display.lesson: We remember sad days in order to learn and improve; as long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, Hashem guards us.
